llm.summary: The skill has a coherent brand-knowledge-base purpose, but it sends full uploaded materials to an external LLM and automatically keeps a raw source bundle, which users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is limited to user-supplied paths under the workspace or skill directory, and there is no evidence of shell execution, tool hijacking, persistence hooks, or unrelated system access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest discloses OPENAI_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_BASE_URL, and external API transfer of full provided materials; requirements pin PDF and dotenv dependencies flagged by the scanner as vulnerable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks for business documents and contact/compliance details, but the first-use instructions and intake template do not clearly warn users at the collection point that full inputs will be sent to the configured external LLM provider.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code automatically writes source_bundle.md containing the raw compiled input materials to the output directory, but the SKILL export list does not disclose that raw source retention behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the code: it collects brand materials or an intake form, extracts a structured brand package, generates FAQ/glossary/messaging assets, and exports local files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending the full contents of provided brand materials to the configured OpenAI-compatible API provider and keeping a raw source_bundle.md in the output. Do not upload secrets, confidential customer records, regulated data, or unredacted transcripts unless your organization approves that handling. Consider updating vulnerable pinned dependencies before processing PDFs.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the code reads OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL from environment variables for the disclosed LLM API integration; I found no SSH, browser, cloud credential store, or broad credential harvesting behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in part: collecting brand, contact, and compliance information is expected, and the manifest/README disclose external LLM processing, but the runtime first-use and intake instructions under-disclose this before asking for materials.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: main.py automatically writes the full raw compiled input into source_bundle.md, creating extra retention of potentially confidential source materials beyond the documented export list.
[SC4] unexpected: Accepted as a dependency risk signal: requirements.txt pins pypdf==4.3.1 and python-dotenv==1.0.0, and the skill processes user-supplied PDFs, making parser denial-of-service concerns relevant.
[LP3] expected: Mostly downgraded: although SKILL.md itself lacks a formal permissions boundary, manifest.json declares environment variables and network transfer, and main.py enforces workspace/skill-directory path checks for inputs and outputs.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security verdict: the Chinese-default prompts and templates affect usability/locale behavior, but they are visible and consistent with the package content rather than deceptive or high-impact security behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded: API credentials and network-backed model processing are reflected in manifest.json and README.md, so this is infrastructure required for the advertised extraction workflow.
